title_en: Not All Entropy Is Equal: Reward-Conditioned Entropy Allocation in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
title_zh: 并非所有熵都平等：可验证奖励强化学习中的奖励条件熵分配
summary_en: The paper introduces Reward-Conditioned Entropy Allocation (RCEA), a hierarchical diagnostic framework for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) that separates complete-trajectory entropy from average token entropy, conditions uncertainty on verifier outcome and process validity, and measures correct-solution-mode retention. Controlled sweeps over six RLVR objectives at two model scales show that entropy trajectories do not induce a stable ordering of reasoning accuracy. Token entropy is higher for verifier-failed than successful trajectories, with paired analysis confidence intervals excluding equality at 10 of 12 endpoints. A local covariance approximation predicts the direction of adjacent-checkpoint entropy change in 95.5% of nonfailed transitions, and a reward-stratified endpoint proxy shows positive chosen-token covariance is more tail-concentrated within failed prefixes.
summary_zh: 本文提出了奖励条件熵分配（RCEA），一种分层诊断框架，用于可验证奖励强化学习（RLVR），将完整轨迹熵与平均令牌熵分离，根据验证器结果和过程有效性条件化不确定性，并测量正确解模式的保留。在两个模型规模上对六种RLVR目标进行控制扫描发现，熵轨迹不会导致推理准确性的稳定排序。验证器失败的轨迹的令牌熵高于成功轨迹，配对分析置信区间在12个端点中的10个排除相等。局部协方差近似在95.5%的非失败转换中预测了相邻检查点熵变化的方向，奖励分层端点代理进一步表明，正选择令牌协方差在失败前缀内更集中于尾部。
content_en: Policy entropy is widely used to diagnose exploration and collapse in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), yet its magnitude does not consistently track reasoning performance across optimization objectives. We argue that this ambiguity arises because global token entropy conflates uncertainty in successful and failed trajectories, diversity across correct solution strategies, and variation among realizations of the same strategy. We introduce \textbf{Reward-Conditioned Entropy Allocation (RCEA)}, a hierarchical diagnostic framework that separates complete-trajectory entropy from average token entropy, conditions uncertainty on verifier outcome and process validity, measures correct-solution-mode retention, and connects these population-level quantities to local covariance-driven updates. In controlled sweeps over six RLVR objectives at two model scales, entropy trajectories do not induce a stable ordering of reasoning accuracy. Token entropy is higher for verifier-failed than successful trajectories under both broad separately aggregated estimates and a common-question paired analysis, whose confidence intervals exclude equality at 10 of 12 displayed endpoints. A local covariance approximation predicts the direction of adjacent-checkpoint entropy change in 95.5\% of nonfailed transitions; a reward-stratified endpoint proxy further shows that positive chosen-token covariance is more tail-concentrated within failed prefixes.
